correctness.rationale: The weighted Laplacian splits orthogonally into two within-class zero-sum eigenspaces and the between-class sign eigenspace. Explicit pseudoinverse yields all within- and cross-column entries with multiplicities, identifying the only current sign change at x=1. Factored rational differences rigorously yield all phase regimes, including n=5 crossover x=3/7. Reciprocal comparisons exclude subunit conductance from global optima except the exactly paired n=3 cycle optimum; differentiation gives unique critical points and exact quadratic-form maxima. Independent grounded-Laplacian inversion confirms all 3285 columns in 54 exact rational cases. Infinite claims follow from the displayed algebra, not numerical extrapolation.

Two general electrical-localization full-text sources bound transfer-current operators but do not imply the exact two-block weighted endpoint norms or their maximizing-edge transitions. Previously accessible statements about weighted perfect matching and unit complete multipartite results do not contain the dense two-community conductance family; targeted public-record searches returned no stronger exact counterpart. Residual unindexed electrical calculations remain possible, so uniqueness is not asserted.

value.rationale: A canonical and motivated two-community weighted complete network undergoes a full classifiable endpoint-operator phase diagram. The unique size-five cross–within–cross reentrance, a reciprocal pair of cycle-optimal weights only at size three, and different global conductance optimizers for complementary projections are genuine finite/infinite structural information. Optimized norms remain uniformly bounded by 1+sqrt5 and 2+sqrt5 across all sizes, in contrast with other heterogeneously weighted complete-graph models. It is neither a unit-weight table lookup nor a direct generic spectral bound.
